chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever denies the faith, his work indeed would be Confiscated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Neglecting the deed which he had acknowledged with it. From that is if he were to neglect the Salat from without an illness or a pre-occupation'.

key_terms.حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ: His work/deeds were nullified or voided

ai.seo_question: What does 'denying the faith' mean in the context of neglecting prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'denial of faith' (Kufr) in the context of nullifying deeds is not limited to theological disbelief, but includes the practical negation of core obligations. He specifically identifies the neglect of prayer without a valid excuse (such as illness or preoccupation) as the primary manifestation of this denial, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of belief and ritual practice.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ubeyd, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:5] and whoever denies the faith, his work indeed would be Confiscated. Heasws said: ‘Neglecting the deed which he had acknowledged with it. From that is if he were to neglect the Salāt from without an illness or a pre-occupation’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Ubayd from Zurara who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘The deeds of anyone who rejects belief, certainly, become fruitless. He, on the Day of Judgment will be of those who lose.’ [5:5] The Imam said, ‘It is disregarding the deeds that he has confessed to be true. Of such deeds is disregarding prayer without suffering from illness or being preoccupied. ’”
